findings.reason: the section's headline comparison would otherwise be gated on a population of 37 the plan has already proven unmeasurable, and the worker must either fail the bullet or silently drop two families.
findings.text: §5's second bullet requires the reading "on the 37 families of the blind sheet that both readers gave the same domain ... measured in the same run", but the §2 comparison committed with this document change measured 35: `labelled-comparison.json` carries `sheet_families_mapping_to_more_than_one_decision_family` with 2 entries (item-077 `<X>_current_density_due_to_<X>_viscosity`, item-084 `<X>_coordinate_of_<X>_magnetic_field_probe`), each of which straddles two decision families, so those two agreed sheet families have no single decision to read against; the bullet neither excludes them nor records them, leaving a §5 worker unable to tell a structural floor from a shortfall

findings.reason: the two disputed families are already routed to `g-sdpf-disputed-items` and the six agreed families sit inside the 35 measured, so both the declaration and the dispatch stand; only the commentary's arithmetic is wrong.
findings.text: the §2 close comment states "five of the eight families §1 names carry a label both readers agree on; two of the other three are among the twelve disputed items awaiting the lead's ruling", but the committed sheet holds all eight and its two readers agree on six (item-001, item-052, item-054, item-073, item-104 and item-113 agree; only item-006 and item-053 differ), and `labelled-comparison.json`'s own `section_one_families_measured` reads 5 while its 35 `family_rows` contain six §1 patterns, so the record both understates the coverage and implies an eighth family carrying no label at all
